title: Dentist
content: Reschedule dentist for next month. Insurance reset Jan 1 so the cleaning should be covered.

title: Furnace filter
content: Furnace filter model MX-2200, 16x25x1. Buy two, swap every 90 days. Hardware store on Woodward has them.

title: Realization at standup
content: Sat in the suspension review this morning and realized I haven't actually enjoyed designing wheel hubs in about four years. I'm good at it. I just don't care. That's a weird thing to admit to yourself in a conference room.

title: Groceries
content: Milk, eggs, the bread Ethan likes (not the seedy one), coffee, dish soap. Lisa wants the oat milk this time.

title: Talked to Raj
content: Long call with Raj tonight. He switched into tech at 36, said the first year was brutal — felt like the dumbest person in every room. But zero regrets. He's L4 at Google now. Said the thing that mattered most was shipping a real project, not the certificates. Kept saying 'just build stuff.'

title: Daycare invoice
content: Ethan's daycare invoice came in — $1,240 this month. Up from last year. Lisa flagged it.

title: Bootcamp math
content: Codesmith Detroit is $14k, 6 months full-time. We have ~$42k saved. If I quit, household drops to Lisa's ~$35k. Six months of mortgage ($1,750) + living + tuition... math is tight but possible. Maybe. The ISA option means no tuition up front but you pay a chunk of salary later. Need to actually run the numbers instead of doing this in my head at 11pm.

title: Kitchen paint
content: Lisa wants to repaint the kitchen. Beige or sage. I genuinely do not have an opinion but apparently 'I don't care' is the wrong answer. Sage, I guess.

title: Django project
content: Got auth working on the expense tracker tonight. Took three hours and most of it was a stupid CSRF thing but when the login finally worked I was grinning at my laptop at midnight like an idiot. I do not grin at wheel hubs.

title: Car insurance
content: Renewal up 12%. Call and ask about bundling with the home policy. Possibly shop around.

title: Imposter thought
content: The thought that won't leave: will anyone actually hire a 34-year-old mechanical engineer with no CS degree? Or am I going to spend $14k to find out the answer is no. Raj says yes but Raj is one guy.

title: Ethan swim
content: Sign Ethan up for the toddler swim class at the rec center. Saturdays 10am. Spots fill fast per Lisa's mom.

title: Layoffs again
content: Powertrain group lost eight people today. Second round in 18 months. I wasn't touched, neither was my team, but the floor felt like a funeral. Dave said 'we're fine' which is exactly what they said last time. Hard to feel stable here even though stability is supposedly the whole point of this job.

title: Mom's birthday
content: Mom's birthday May 22. Don't forget like last year. Maybe the garden center gift card.

title: Lisa conversation
content: Brought up the bootcamp idea seriously for the first time. Lisa said she'd support whatever I decide. But the way she said it was tight — that flat voice she uses when she's worried but doesn't want a fight. I think she's scared about the money and I don't blame her. I need to bring her a real plan, not a feeling.

title: Oil change
content: CR-V due for oil change, ~78k miles. Also the rear wiper streaks, replace it.

title: freeCodeCamp
content: Finished the responsive web design cert and most of the JS algorithms section on freeCodeCamp. 8 months of evenings now. Some nights I'm too fried after work and Ethan to do anything but it adds up slowly.

title: Gutters
content: Clean the gutters before the spring rains really start. Or pay the guy. Probably pay the guy.

title: Salary gap
content: Caught up with two college friends. One's a backend dev in Chicago clearing ~$165k, the other does data stuff remote, similar. I'm at $98k plus a bonus that shrinks every year. Eleven years in. The gap is hard to look at directly.

title: Ethan checkup
content: Ethan's 3-year checkup Thursday 2pm. Bring the vaccine card. Ask the pediatrician about the molar coming in.

title: Dry cleaning
content: Pick up dry cleaning Thursday. The gray suit and two shirts. Ticket is in the kitchen drawer.

title: What if I hate it
content: Honest 1am fear: what if I love coding as a hobby and hate it as a job? Hobbies don't have standups and Jira and a manager breathing down your neck about a sprint. Maybe the thing I actually love is that nobody's paying me to do it. How would I even test that before betting the family on it?

title: Lawn mower
content: Mower won't start. Probably the spark plug or old gas. Drain the tank, new plug, try again before calling it dead.

title: Dave one-on-one
content: Dave floated a lead engineer path — maybe a year, year and a half out. He means well. He's an automotive lifer and genuinely doesn't understand why I'd look elsewhere. I didn't mention the coding. Felt strange sitting on it.

title: Costco run
content: Costco: diapers (size 5 now), paper towels, the chicken Lisa roasts, batteries, Ethan's fruit pouches. Don't buy another thing we don't need like last time.

title: Portfolio idea
content: If I'm going to convince anyone to hire me, the expense tracker isn't enough. Need one real, polished, deployed project that solves an actual problem. Maybe something using my automotive domain knowledge — a parts/inventory tool? Lean into the thing I already know instead of pretending I'm a fresh grad.

title: HOA email
content: HOA wants the trash bins out of view from the street. Move the bins to the side of the garage. Reply so they stop emailing.

title: Running toward or away
content: Coach-type question I can't shake: am I running toward software, or just running away from being bored in automotive? Because those lead to different plans. If it's 'toward,' a bootcamp makes sense. If it's 'away,' I might just be restless and a new job in any field would scratch it. Don't love that I can't answer this cleanly.

title: Anniversary
content: Wedding anniversary June 21. Book the place on Main that Lisa liked. Ask her mom to take Ethan overnight.

title: Time audit
content: Tried to count my real study hours this week: maybe 6, scattered, mostly after 10pm. At this rate self-study could take another two years to get job-ready, if I don't burn out first. That's the honest case against 'just keep studying on the side.' The slow path isn't risk-free either — it's just a different risk.

title: Everyone says something different
content: Funny thing: I've asked maybe five people and gotten five answers. Raj says just leap. Dave basically thinks the question is crazy. Lisa wants a plan, not a feeling. The finance guy at the gym said the bootcamp's fine on paper but I'd be betting the emergency fund on a timeline I don't control. They're all kind of right, which is useless. Nobody's weighing the same thing — upside, stability, the family, the cash. I keep wishing I could get all of them in one room and make them argue it out until something actually shakes loose.
